column4: Visit note | 2025-09-13 03:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Sanjida Faruque, 67, female. Mrs. Faruque returns for review of her ongoing condition and mentions she continues to feel constantly cold, struggles with dry skin, and feels unusually slow and fatigued. She is a retired civil servant and first found these symptoms during tests for tiredness after moving to Cox's Bazar. She takes her daily tablets consistently. She denies any chest pain, palpitations, or memory lapses. On examination: TSH 16.7 mIU/L, BP 129/73 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 71 kg. Her reflexes are normal and there is no peripheral edema. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued for her ongoing management. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.
